sources.entry: Omniplayer - Best media player on Mac, support almost all format. [![App Store][app-store Icon]](https://apps.apple.com/app/id1470926410?platform=mac)

summary.name: OmniPlayer
summary.one_liner: OmniPlayer is a media player and personal video library app for iOS, macOS and tvOS that plays local and network-drive video and can cast media to smart TVs.
keywords: play wmv flv mov on mac
use_cases: Play MKV, AVI, MOV, WMV and FLAC files on a Mac
Build a personal local movie and TV library
Stream local video to a DLNA, Chromecast or Roku TV
Play YouTube or Vimeo videos without ads
Watch movies from a network or net disk drive
summary.what_it_does:
OmniPlayer plays local and network-stored movie and TV files on Mac, and the page says it supports formats including mp4, mkv, avi, mov, wmv, flv, mp3, flac and ape. It can create a local personal media library. It can cast or mirror local video with subtitles to smart TVs and devices using DLNA, Chromecast or Roku protocols, including Samsung, Sony, LG and Xbox devices named on the page. The page also says it can play YouTube and Vimeo videos without ads. The page describes it as an all-in-one player for iOS, macOS and tvOS.</what_it_does>
<parameter name="pricing">freemium
notable: Casts local video with subtitles to DLNA, Chromecast and Roku devices
Plays YouTube and Vimeo without ads
Supports many formats including MKV, AVI, FLAC and APE
Listed in the awesome-mac list under Audio and Video Tools
caveats: Page shows a $29.99 price with a free trial, so the full version appears to be paid
TV discovery needs the TV and Mac on the same network and no VPN or firewall blocking it
Some video files may not play, and the page offers support contact rather than a guaranteed fix
